translation_notes: prefixes: RDFS->rdfs, DCTERMS->dcterms, PROV->prov, FDOF->fdof, FDOC->fdoc

Same repository, same finding as the ns_import_project sibling test_add_fdo_profile: `from rdflib.namespace import RDFS, DCTERMS, PROV` cannot take `from … import p:` (ldpy/012 point 21 -- rdflib.namespace exports no `__namespaces__`); only DCTERMS is dereferenced in this region's body, so it alone becomes `@prefix dcterms:` (RDFS, PROV drop out, unused here and in original.py). `from nanopub.namespaces import FDOF, FDOC` DOES take `from … import p:`, through a hand-written `nanopub_ns_shim.py` (ldpy/012 point 15bis's sanctioned fix for a real third-party module lacking `__namespaces__`) -- values transcribed verbatim from the installed `nanopub` package's namespaces.py at the pinned commit. FDOF is imported but never dereferenced in this region's body; kept anyway, mirroring the whole import line as one unit, same convention as the sibling's own FDOF.

`self.tuples[pred] = URIRef(uri)` is a dict assignment on `self`, not a graph write -- there is no `@graph`/`+{ }` here, just term construction and prefixed-name dereference (this region's own `categories`: namespace_term 1, term_constructor 1). driver.py calls `set_profile` directly with `self` duck-typed as `types.SimpleNamespace(tuples={})` (compares equal by `__dict__`), so the mutated `self.tuples` dict is the oracle for which predicate `use_fdof` picks.

Fixture-strength check: swapping the two branches (`dcterms:conformsTo if use_fdof else fdoc:hasFdoProfile`) flips `rdfeval check` to FAIL on all three calls (wrong predicate holds the URIRef); reverted afterward, OK confirmed again.
